subject.title: feat: per-agent session visibility and agentToAgent scoping

question: Should OpenClaw expose `agents.list[].tools.sessions.visibility` plus per-agent `agentToAgent` as this PR's public authorization contract, or fold the work into a broader per-capability/bidirectional session policy first?
rationale: The change defines a security-sensitive cross-agent session boundary and overlaps other open policy PRs, so automation cannot safely choose the long-term config contract or consolidation path.

options.title: Require a refreshed complete implementation
options.body: Approve the general per-agent direction, but require this branch to rebase, wire all session tools, add denied history/status coverage, and provide real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Fold into broader policy design
options.body: Pause this PR and consolidate it with the canonical issue's per-capability or receive-side authorization work before exposing new config.

options.title: Prefer narrower PRs first
options.body: Land the proven narrower A2A or sandbox pieces independently and leave this broad PR for a later replacement implementation.

recommendation.title: Require a refreshed complete implementation
recommendation.body: Approve the general per-agent direction, but require this branch to rebase, wire all session tools, add denied history/status coverage, and provide real behavior proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The history and CONTRIBUTING.md routing make steipete the best available owner for a public cross-agent authorization/config decision.
